newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean right backs ex-ambassador against drug charge.
newsitem.headline: Chilean right backs ex-ambassador against drug charge.

text.p: Chilean right-wing politicians on Tuesday rallied around a blue-blood former ambassador to Britain who was arrested for activities allegedly connected to the late Mexican drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
But a senior official of the center-left government suggested that the drug racketeering inquiry was only scratching the surface into Carrillo's contacts in Chile.

Hernan Errazuriz Talavera, a lawyer, businessman and politician who served as Chile's ambassador in London between 1990 and 1993, was detained on Monday on charges stemming from his alleged involvement with members of Carrillo's cartel.
Police also arrested a Mexican woman and three other Chilean men -- a real estate broker, a currency dealer and a chauffeur -- under similar charges.
The former diplomat's brother, Francisco Javier Errazuriz, a multimillionaire senator and former presidential candidate, said the investigation would prove his sibling's innocence.
According to the senator, Hernan Errazuriz only acted as an attorney in a few real estate deals at the request of a broker representing Carrillo's lieutenants.
"You can rest assured that, even though we may not work together in business ventures and are not especially close, I will always love my brothers as brothers," the senator added.
Ironically, the former diplomat was arrested under an antidrug law actively sponsored by his own brother.
Interior Undersecretary Belisario Velasco said it was now up to the courts to rule on Errazuriz's responsibility.
"This has only started in Chile (and) it will take time," he told reporters. "People representing Mr. Carrillo made certain contacts here and they must be properly investigated."

A congressional leader of the center-right Renovacion Nacional party, Claudio Rodriguez, said the former diplomat could hardly have been expected to divine that he was dealing with gangsters when at the same time Chile's police did not know Carrillo was here.
Carrillo, known as "the Lord of the Skies" because he shipped huge loads of cocaine in gutted airliners, lived here for nearly three months this year under a false identity.
Chile's top antidrugs official, Mario Mallea, said on Monday that the Mexican crime boss planned to establish residence in this country, which shares borders with coca- producing Bolivia and Peru.
He bought mansions and a fleet of luxury cars in Santiago. However, in June he traveled to Cuba and Mexico, where he died on July 4 after undergoing massive plastic surgery.
